cases.situation: My colleague Kim just sent the all-company email for Friday's town hall, and the Zoom link goes to last month's meeting, which is expired. She's a peer.
cases.reply: Hey Kim, quick heads up: the Zoom link in the town hall email goes to last month's meeting and shows as expired when I click it. Easy fix with a quick resend. Happens to all of us!
cases.note: Private DM, straight away, one plain sentence, then move on.

cases.situation: 好朋友小雨最近口气有点重，下周三我们要一起做模拟面试，我觉得应该告诉她。想私下发微信。
cases.reply: 有件小事有点不好意思开口，但换成是我也希望你告诉我：最近你说话时口气有点重，可能是上火或者牙齿的问题，面试前去看看牙医也许有帮助。就这个，没别的啦，周三模拟面试见！
cases.note: 只说一次、私下说、给个可能的原因，然后马上转到别的话题。

cases.situation: I manage a small warehouse office team. One of my reports, Derek, has had noticeable body odour for a few weeks and two people have mentioned it to me. I need to raise it with him privately.
cases.reply: Derek, can I raise something a bit personal? It stays between us. Over the last few weeks I've noticed a body odour at times, mostly in the afternoons. I'm not assuming anything about the reason. If something's going on, a health thing or something at home, tell me and we'll work out what helps. Otherwise, can we agree you'll keep an eye on it, and that's the end of it?
cases.note: Never mention that others complained. Say it once, in person, and don't bring it up again if it's fixed.

cases.situation: My director Helen is presenting to the board on Zoom right now and she's sharing her whole screen. Her Slack notifications keep popping up in the corner, including one from HR about restructuring. I'm in the meeting.
cases.reply: Helen, your Slack notifications are showing on the shared screen. Sharing just the slides window will hide them, it catches everyone on Zoom.
cases.note: Senior person, live meeting: private chat, one line, the fix included, and never mention what the notification said.

cases.situation: I told my gym buddy Marcus, privately, that there's been a strong smell after our sessions lately. He replied 'wow, ok, thanks for that I guess' and has been short with me since. We train together Tuesdays and Thursdays.
cases.reply: Marcus, I didn't mean to upset you. I only said it because I'd want someone to tell me. That's all, I won't mention it again. Still on for Thursday at 6?
cases.note: When they get defensive, don't repeat the details or add evidence. One line, then straight back to normal.

cases.situation: A teammate who joined six weeks ago, Tom, keeps calling me Nicole. My name is Nicola. I let it go too long and he's now said it in meetings a dozen times. We get on well.
cases.reply: Hey Tom, tiny thing: it's Nicola, not Nicole. Really easy mix-up, and I should have said something weeks ago! See you at standup.
cases.note: Private, one line, and share the blame for the delay so he doesn't feel he's been embarrassing himself for weeks. Never mention it again.
